blocker.summary: r467 attempted the live gdb session r466 named (breaking on the movie-worker KeWaitForMultipleObjects return to inspect which wait object stays permanently signaled) but did not reach that state, and characterized three separate environment obstacles instead of guessing past them. (1) ptrace_scope=1 with no root closes attaching to a normal run_gate.py-launched process (not this session's direct child). (2) Launching directly under gdb (the only attach path without root) surfaces a real, reproducible SIGSEGV in rex_sub_821E4378 (real recompiled PPC game code) on the Main XThread that never occurs in a normal non-debugger launch -- consistent with the engine relying on its own SIGSEGV handling for some internal mechanism that a debugger intercepting the signal breaks; adding 'handle SIGSEGV nostop noprint pass' avoids the crash but massively slows execution. (3) That slowdown exceeds this harness's background-task time budget, which killed the process before it ever reached the target breakpoint (twice, reproducibly). A static search for the three movie-worker addresses in the generated PPC C++ found zero literal occurrences, as expected -- XenonRecomp/ReXGlue computes most data addresses via runtime register arithmetic, not baked-in literals, so this is not evidence the addresses don't exist, just that this particular static search can't find them. Root cause remains NOT established. Cleanup was thorough: all orphaned ac6recomp/gdb/Xvfb processes killed, and the native profile's build state was fully restored and reverified (ctest 11/11, live probe identical to the r454-r466 baseline, no regression) -- the rexglue-oracle-profile work this cycle only ever touched the shared manifest.json/static-validation.json path temporarily. Named for r468: two options, not yet chosen between -- (a) a Ghidra headless pass on the ac6-us project to find the two XEvents' creation sites via static data cross-references, avoiding a long debugger-attached process entirely; (b) first investigate, without gdb, why rex_sub_821E4378 never crashes in a normal launch, which might unblock a faster future gdb session by removing the SIGSEGV noise entirely. Still open, non-blocking: (1) the pinned shader registry coverage gap (r456) remains the main track once this is resolved; (2) once PinnedShaderRuntime wiring is judged mature, reconsider the native backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454-r462); (3) update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path (r452/r453, convenience only).
